animals.name: phylum: Porifera
animals.traits: no body symmetry, oskulum and ostia, sessile - attached to a substrate

animals.name: class: Hydrozoa
animals.traits:
two stages
- polyp (sessile): longass tentacles
- medusa (mobile): u know what a medusa looks like bro

animals.name: class: Turbellaria
animals.traits: flat body, bilateral symmetry, three branches of intestine, mouth+anus - the light spot in the middle of their body

animals.name: class: Trematoda
animals.traits: bilateral symmetry, flat body, leaf-like shape, two suckers: oral and ventral

animals.name: class: Monogenea
animals.traits: bilateral symmetry, flat body, most species under 2cm, suction target - opisthaptor (suction cups + hooks)

animals.name: class: Cestoda
animals.traits: bilateral symmetry, flat body, usually segmented, long - up to 20m, visible head with suckers and hooks

animals.name: phylum: Syndermata
animals.traits: bro idk just pray this shit isnt there ig

animals.name: subclass: Caenogastropoda
animals.traits:
leg, spiraled shell, just snail features HOWEVER!! specifics compared to heterobranchia
- they have a lid on the shell called operculum, or some weirdass marine shell with a slim opening

animals.name: order: Basommatophora
animals.traits:
gastropoda: one leg, one spiral shell, tentacles 
basommatophora: one pair of tentacles they DONT have eyes on the tentacles but at the base, shell either flat or fat spiral with a spiked tip (its exact species ull just prolly have to learn by heart)

animals.name: order: Stylommatophora
animals.traits:
gastropoda: one leg, one spiral shell, tentacles 
stylommatophora: four tentacles, eyes are ON THE TIPS, normal garden snails, slugs, could have weird ass appendages on the openingg of the shell or litteral hair or spiked shell

animals.name: class: Bivalvia
animals.traits: one leg, attached to substrate yk, TWO FLAT SHELLS, if u cant tell this apart ur cooked man

animals.name: class: Polychaeta
animals.traits:
poly - many
annelida: ringed worms - segmented body 
polychaeta: mostly marine, pair of parapodia on every segment + visible bristles, modified parapodia into antenae

animals.name: class: Oligochaeta
animals.traits:
oligos - few, chaite - bristles
annelida: ringed worms - segmented body 
oligochaeta: no parapoda - 2 pairs of bristles on each segment, visible clitellum (only in adults though), head with literally nothing on it

animals.name: class: Hirudinea
animals.traits:
annelida: ringed worms - segmented body 
hirudinea: 34 segments, 2 suckers (head + ass), 1-5 pairs of eyes

animals.name: phylum: Nematoda
animals.traits: smooth, no segments, perfectly round body, sum spike on da ass

animals.name: order: Anostraca
animals.traits:
ano - without, straca - shell
crustacea: head+thorax+abdomen or cephalothorax+abdomen, segmented body and limbs
cl. branchiopoda: leafy limbs with gills, abdomen WITHOUT legs
anostraca: 11 pairs of limbs, males with large antenae, 2 compound eyes on stems + 3RD EYE on forehead lol, no shell, swim on their back

animals.name: order: Notostraca
animals.traits:
notum - dosal 
crustacea: head+thorax+abdomen or cephalothorax+abdomen, segmented body and limbs
cl. branchiopoda: leafy limbs with gills, abdomen WITHOUT legs
anostraca: 11 pairs of limbs, males with large antenae, 2 compound eyes on stems + 3RD EYE on forehead lol, no shell, swim on their back

animals.name: order: Cladocera
animals.traits:
cladon - branched, ceros - horn
crustacea: head+thorax+abdomen or cephalothorax+abdomen, segmented body and limbs
cl. branchiopoda: leafy limbs with gills, abdomen WITHOUT legs
cladostera: big ass antenae with stems, round, laterally flattened, carapace folded, one compound  eye, stinger at the ass

animals.name: subclass: Branchiura
animals.traits:
brankhion - gill, oura - tail
crustacea: head+thorax+abdomen or cephalothorax+abdomen, segmented body and limbs
cl. maxillopoda: max 6 segments on thorax, no limbs on abdomen
branchiura: 4 pairs of limbs, abdomen no segments, suckers and stinger, 5-25mm, 2 eyes on dorsal side

animals.name: subclass: Pentastomida
animals.traits:
penta - 5, stoma - mouth
crustacea: head+thorax+abdomen or cephalothorax+abdomen, segmented body and limbs
cl. maxillopoda: max 6 segments on thorax, no limbs on abdomen
pentastomida: 2-13cm, worm-like segmented body, 4 hooks + mouth on head

animals.name: subclass: Copepoda
animals.traits:
cope - paddle
crustacea: head+thorax+abdomen or cephalothorax+abdomen, segmented body and limbs
cl. maxillopoda: max 6 segments on thorax, no limbs on abdomen
copepoda: 2mm, 1st pair of antenae super long, one naupli eye, large head shield, head+thorax+abdomen, forked tail

animals.name: order: Decapoda
animals.traits:
crustacea: head+thorax+abdomen or cephalothorax+abdomen, segmented body and limbs
cl. malostraca: carapax with Ca, legs also on abdomen
decapoda: 10 pairs of limbs, 4th pair pincers, head and thorax fused - one segment of carapax, stemmed eyes

animals.name: order: Isopoda
animals.traits:
iso - same
crustacea: head+thorax+abdomen or cephalothorax+abdomen, segmented body and limbs
cl. malostraca: carapax with Ca, legs also on abdomen
isopoda: head fused with first thorax segment, 7 segments thorax + 6 seg. abdomen, similar legs but different in size, compound eyes on head NOT stemmed

animals.name: order: Amphipoda
animals.traits:
amphi - of both kinds
crustacea: head+thorax+abdomen or cephalothorax+abdomen, segmented body and limbs
cl. malostraca: carapax with Ca, legs also on abdomen
amphipoda: head fused with first thorax segment, 7 segments thorax + 6 seg. abdomen, latteraly flattened, some legs are pincer-like, bad posture - shrimp-like, eyes not stemmed

animals.name: class: Xiphosura
animals.traits:
chelicerata: head and thorax - prosoma, abdomen - opistosoma, 1pair chelicera, 1pair pedipalps and 4pairs of walking limbs
xiphosura: prosoma n opisoma shields, tail, long pedipalps

animals.name: order: Scorpionida
animals.traits:
chelicerata: head and thorax - prosoma, abdomen - opistosoma, 1pair chelicera, 1pair pedipalps and 4pairs of walking limbs
scorpionida: three-parts on cheliceras, pincers on pedipalps, two parts of abdomen - normal and movable one, posionous gland with telson

animals.name: order: Pseudoscorpionida
animals.traits:
chelicerata: head and thorax - prosoma, abdomen - opistosoma, 1pair chelicera, 1pair pedipalps and 4pairs of walking limbs
pseudoscorpionida: two parts in chelicers, pedipalps with poison glands, no tail

animals.name: order: Acari
animals.traits:
chelicerata: head and thorax - prosoma, abdomen - opistosoma, 1pair chelicera, 1pair pedipalps and 4pairs of walking limbs
acari: abdomen and thorax fused - head and body basically, small - less then 1mm

animals.name: order: Opilionida
animals.traits:
chelicerata: head and thorax - prosoma, abdomen - opistosoma, 1pair chelicera, 1pair pedipalps and 4pairs of walking limbs
opilionida: DADDY LONG LEGS, prosoma and broadly connected to segmented optisoma - oval body, pseudosegmented legs, 1 pair of eyes

animals.name: order: Araneida
animals.traits:
chelicerata: head and thorax - prosoma, abdomen - opistosoma, 1pair chelicera, 1pair pedipalps and 4pairs of walking limbs
araneida: 8 eyes, prosoma visibly connected to nonsegmented optisoma by pedicel

animals.name: class: Chilopoda
animals.traits:
myriapoda: head + trunk (14-177 segments), at least 9 pairs of limbs
chilopoda (centipedes): long antennae, 1 pair of legs on each trunk segment, legs on the sides of the body, last pair of legs prolonged, limbs on the 1st trunk segment = maxillipeds with venom glands, fast runners, mostly predatory

animals.name: suborder: Anisoptera
animals.traits:
hexapoda: head + thorax (3 segments) + abdomen, 6 legs (1 pair on each thorax segment)
odonata: predators, short antennae, ocelli, wings with pterostigma (+ nodus)
anisoptera (dragonflies): eyes very close, hind wings with anal lobes, wings not folded, more robust/fat abdomen

animals.name: order: Lepidoptera
animals.traits:
hexapoda: head + thorax (3 segments) + abdomen, 6 legs (1 pair on each thorax segment)
lepidoptera (moths and butterflies): 2 pairs of wings with scales, proboscis, long legs
larva = caterpillar: legs + prolegs, mandibles

animals.name: class: Diplopoda
animals.traits:
myriapoda: head + trunk (14-177 segments), at least 9 pairs of limbs
diplopoda (millipedes): short antennae, legs under the body, 1st segment no legs, 2nd-4th segments 1 pair, the remaining segments (diplosomites) 2 pairs of legs, maxillae fused into a gnathochilarium, slow, mostly detritivorous, can roll up (volvation)
pill millipede (Glomeris) x pill bug (Isopoda): count the leg pairs per segment

animals.name: class: Collembola
animals.traits:
hexapoda: head + thorax (3 segments) + abdomen, 6 legs (1 pair on each thorax segment)
collembola (springtails): minute to 9 mm, entognathous (mouthparts hidden inside the head capsule), 1st segment with a ventral tube (collophore), 3rd-4th segment with a jumping fork (furca), ocelli or blind

animals.name: subclass: Archaeognatha
animals.traits:
hexapoda: head + thorax (3 segments) + abdomen, 6 legs (1 pair on each thorax segment)
archaeognatha (jumping bristletails): mandible with a single joint, large compound eyes that touch each other + ocelli, long maxillary palps, up to 15 mm, covered in scales, styli on the abdomen, 1 epiproct (caudal filament) + 1 pair of cerci all pointing the same way, nocturnal, on rocks, jumpers

animals.name: order: Zygentoma
animals.traits:
hexapoda: head + thorax (3 segments) + abdomen, 6 legs (1 pair on each thorax segment)
zygentoma (silverfish): wingless (never had wings), up to 10 mm, covered in scales, one colour, compound eyes apart or missing, styli only on the last 2 abdominal segments, epiproct + 1 pair of cerci pointing to the sides, much smaller maxillary palps, do not jump, omnivorous, pests

animals.name: order: Ephemeroptera
animals.traits:
pterygota: 2 pairs of wings; paleoptera: wings not folded on the abdomen
ephemeroptera (mayflies): short antennae, 2 long cerci (sometimes + 1 terminal filament), adult does not feed and lives 1 day, subimago = cloudy wings + fuzzy body
nymphs: in water, tracheal gills, 3 caudal filaments

animals.name: suborder: Zygoptera
animals.traits:
hexapoda: head + thorax (3 segments) + abdomen, 6 legs (1 pair on each thorax segment)
odonata: predators, short antennae, ocelli, wings with pterostigma (+ nodus)
zygoptera (damselflies): eyes apart, wings with stems, folded along the abdomen (not touching), slim

animals.name: order: Plecoptera
animals.traits:
neoptera (polyneoptera): chewing mouthparts, wings folded on the abdomen, usually a large anal lobe on the wings
plecoptera (stoneflies): cloudy wings folded over each other horizontally, 2 long cerci, long antennae, ocelli, good runners
nymphs: 2 cerci (x Ephemeroptera), gills near the legs, abdomen, mouth

animals.name: order: Blattodea
animals.traits:
neoptera (polyneoptera): chewing mouthparts, wings folded on the abdomen
blattodea (cockroaches): winged or wingless, leathery front wings = tegmens, multisegmented cerci, large pronotum, massive coxae, thorny tibiae, eggs in an ootheca, usually night-active

animals.name: order: Mantodea
animals.traits:
neoptera (polyneoptera): chewing mouthparts, wings folded on the abdomen
mantodea (mantises): tegmens, ootheca, hypognathous head, raptorial forelegs, prolonged prothorax, short segmented cerci, males sometimes winged, females apterous

animals.name: suborder: Ensifera
animals.traits:
orthoptera: jumping hind legs, tegmens, 1-segmented cerci, stridulatory and hearing organs
ensifera (crickets and half of the grasshoppers): long antennae, long sword-like ovipositor, hearing organ on the front tibiae, stridulate by rubbing the front wings together, often predatory
